name: fgrowth.data.frame
title: Percentage growth, scale times the lagged ratio minus one. logdiff uses the log difference.

origin.description: Percentage growth, scale times the lagged ratio minus one. logdiff uses the log difference.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector, a matrix, or a data frame given as a dict of columns.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Lag length. A negative value leads. Several lengths return one column each.

arguments.name: diff
arguments.text: How many times to apply the difference or growth.

arguments.name: g
arguments.text: A grouping vector. Levels are sorted.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Not translated. Passing a time index raises CollapseError.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Value written where a lag is missing, or where a cumulative sum would skip a missing value.

arguments.name: logdiff
arguments.text: When true, growth is scale times the log difference.

arguments.name: scale
arguments.text: Multiplier for growth. The default is 100.

arguments.name: power
arguments.text: Power applied to the lagged ratio before subtracting one.

arguments.name: stubs
arguments.text: Accepted for compatibility. Several lags are named L1, F1, and so on.

origin.details: Percentage growth, scale times the lagged ratio minus one. logdiff uses the log difference. A time index, TRA, and grouped data frames are not included. A grouped lag reads the row n places back after that group has been seen n times.
origin.value: A numeric vector, matrix, or data frame of the same length.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(collapse))
x <- c(1, NA, 3, 4, 5, NA)
g <- c("b", "a", "b", "a", "b", "a")
m <- matrix(c(1, NA, 3, 4, 5, 6), nrow = 3)
d <- data.frame(y = c(1, NA, 3), x = c(4, 5, 6))
gm <- c("b", "a", "b")
grab <- function(obj) {
  vals <- if (is.data.frame(obj)) as.numeric(unlist(obj, use.names = FALSE)) else as.numeric(obj)
  ifelse(is.na(vals), "NA", sprintf("%.17g", vals))
}

print(fgrowth.data.frame(d))
